title: Autohandoff priority calibrator and compact telemetry sampler
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: On-call handoffs are noisy and current priority tags are static. Teams repeatedly rebalance duty weights manually after high-traffic windows resulting in inconsistent alert routing and unfair pager distribution. This PR adds an automatic priority calibrator for handoff cards and a compact telemetry sampler that reduces event payloads while preserving incident fidelity. Motivation: reduce on-call cognitive load, stabilize priority ordering during shift boundaries, and cut downstream telemetry costs without losing triage signal. What this PR does (high level): - Introduces a priority-calibration service that computes a calibrated priority score per responder based on recent response latency, current active incidents, past on-call load (rolling 7d), and soft-capacity (user-configurable). - Adds an adaptive telemetry sampler that reduces per-attachment payload by switching to summary-mode for non-incident windows and high-volume teams; it keeps high-fidelity (full traces/logs) when the calibrator flags a responder or team as incident-relevant. - Implements a feature flag ff_autohandoff_v1 and a staged rollout plan (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with canary checks. - Provides migration notes and a single safe default (no change to routing until flag is enabled). Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for calibrator score logic and edge cases - [x] Integration test for sampler flow with synthetic high-volume and quiet windows - [x] Canary rollout gating by metrics (median response latency, dropped attachments) - [x] Docs: runbook and operational playbook entries added - [x] Backwards compatibility: old priority tag preserved as metadata field Implementation notes: - Calibrator runs as a lightweight worker in incident-bot with per-team caching and TTL=30s to limit churn. - Scoring function is tunable via team settings: weights for latency, active_incidents, historical_load. Defaults chosen after offline simulation (see ENG-11234 notes). - Sampler is implemented in Go in telemetry/pipeline with two modes: full and compact. A probabilistic admission ensures a minimum of 0.5% full fidelity per 1k events to support downstream ML and postmortem sampling needs. - The PR contains a migration job (idempotent) that annotates existing handoff records with calibrated_priority=null to allow a gradual backfill. Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to staging, run smoke and load tests (staging metrics targets documented in ENG-11234). 2) Enable ff_autohandoff_v1 for 10% of teams for 24 hours; monitor: response latency p50/p95, sample-droprate, unit test and integration test stability. 3) If stable, increase to 50% and then 100%. Safety gates and rollback: - If dropped_attachments > 0.2% above baseline or responder-misroutes detected, immediately revert flag via console. - Feature toggle supports per-team opt-out. Observability and dashboards added: - New dashboards: "Handoff Priority Distribution", "Telemetry Sampler Loss Rate", "Calibrator Decision Log (sampled)". - Alerts: sampler_drop_rate > 0.3% sustained for 30m; calibrator_score_flip_rate > 2% per hour. Related work and references: - Linear: ENG-11234 (simulation + weight tuning), PM-458 (product acceptance criteria). - Internal doc: /docs/oncall/autohandoff-design.md Testing: - 34 new unit tests (Python), 6 Go integration tests. - A small chaos test that simulates burst alerts and verifies sampler retains at least 1 sample per 2000 events per team. Migration and backwards compatibility: - No forced migrations; existing handoffs keep old_priority tag. - Backfill migration annotates records but can be skipped. - API is additive: clients continue to read priority field; calibrated_priority is optional. Security and data governance: - Sampler preserves hashes for dedup and supports PII redaction rules in compact mode. - No telemetry leaves region boundaries; respects regional KMS settings. Rollback steps (quick): - Flip ff_autohandoff_v1 to off -> worker stops emitting calibrated_priority -> sampler switches to full mode for flagged teams -> run revert backfill if needed. Notes for reviewers: - The calibrator scoring function is intentionally conservative; weight defaults are documented and can be tuned via admin UI. - I included micro-benchmarks for worker overhead under 1000 req/s per instance. Please check the canary gating thresholds and the safety alerts.

review_comments: Liam Patel: Nice work — scoring looks sensible. Two asks: make the latency weight configurable per-team and add a guard when historical_load data is missing.
Maya Chen: addressed both: added 'missing_data_fallback' to schema and exposed latency_weight via team settings. pushed a new commit.
Sofia Martinez: Integration test is flaky on CI (sampler admission probabilistic). Can we deterministic-seed the test and add a retry?
Maya Chen: updated integration test to use a deterministic RNG seed and added a retry for the admitted-sample assertion. CI rerun requested.
Noah Gupta: Approved after verifying dashboards and alert thresholds in staging. Left a minor nit about log verbosity level.
Ops (automated): Canary gating reference metrics registered: handoff_median_latency, sampler_drop_rate.
release_notes: Incident-bot: Add autohandoff priority calibrator and adaptive telemetry sampler behind ff_autohandoff_v1. Provides smarter handoff ordering and reduces telemetry costs. Rollout is gated by canary metrics; no behavior change until flag enabled.
notes_for_operators: Feature flag: ff_autohandoff_v1; default OFF; use console to toggle per-team
Key dashboards: Handoff Priority Distribution, Telemetry Sampler Loss Rate
Rollback: flip feature flag off and trigger revert_backfill job if needed
